title: Read center or radius from standard form (or write the equation)
subtitle: Circles · 22 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **22 of the official questions in Circles are this one** — 1 Easy, 10 Medium, 11 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You see an equation already in the form (x − h)² + (y − k)² = number, or you are given a center and radius and the choices are four such equations.
- The question asks for the center, the radius, the diameter, or which equation matches.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Flip the signs inside the brackets to get the center: (x − 3) means h = 3, and (x + 3) means h = −3.
- 2) Take the square root of the right-hand side to get r.
- If the question asks for the diameter, double r.
- 3) To write the equation, put h and k in with flipped signs and square the radius on the right.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type the equation exactly as given.
The circle appears, and you can click its leftmost and rightmost points, or its top and bottom points, to read off the center and the diameter.
For match-the-equation questions, graph each choice and see which one has the right center and size.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You report the right-hand side as the radius without taking its square root, or you keep the signs from inside the brackets so the center comes out with the wrong signs.
On diameter questions, you give the radius and stop.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You report the right-hand side as the radius without taking its square root, or you keep the signs from inside the brackets so the center comes out with the wrong signs.
On diameter questions, you give the radius and stop.
